$comment: Record classes this SDK registers that the BRIDGE rule does not reach. A GATE INPUT, not a filter: scripts/build-record-types.mjs adds these to the derived population while cascade:RecordClass is absent from the pinned spec, and tests/record-types/derivation.test.ts fails when an entry stops being needed. The whole file goes when the marker lands -- not one entry at a time.
$rule: THE RULE THIS FILE WAS WRITTEN AGAINST HAS BEEN RULED OUT. It read: a class whose rdfs:subClassOf chain reaches prov:Entity or prov:Activity holds record data. jayostis/spec#34 (ASK-05) settled that it does not -- "The axiom is PROV-O alignment ... never on prov:Entity, which will keep catching alignment axioms" -- and measured on spec main, 110 classes are in that population while 96 are alignment axioms. The replacement is cascade:RecordClass, a marker the record-bearing classes carry directly, which jayostis/spec#50 adds to the six stable ontologies for 83 classes. Until that revision is pinned here, the build falls back to the old chain plus this list and prints which rule it used.
$established: 2026-09-02, against the prov reading. REVISED 2026-09-03: spec#50 was rewritten after ASK-05 and no longer asks for one rdfs:subClassOf axiom per class -- it adds cascade:RecordClass and marks 83 classes with it, and explicitly forbids adding or removing a prov axiom to change what the gate sees. So these twelve entries are no longer a list of classes awaiting an axiom; they are the classes the superseded bridge cannot see, and the file is deleted whole when the marker is pinned rather than shrinking entry by entry.

entries.detail: clinical:LabResult, the class this deprecated and replaced, declares rdfs:subClassOf prov:Entity. The deprecation moved every lab result out of the coverage gate's population.

The consumer-reported social history. Its clinical: sibling declares cascade:HealthRecord, which itself declares nothing, so both halves of the collision are outside the population for different reasons.

Indistinguishable in the graph from cascade:Address, which is a value structure and correctly NOT a record type: both are a bare owl:Class with an rdfs:label. That pair is the clearest statement of why this rule matters.
Registered since the 2026-08-27 vocabulary wave. Written as its own subject with its own IRI rather than a blank node, so it is stored record data by the same argument as everything else here.

entries.declares: rdfs:subClassOf cascade:HealthRecord, which declares nothing itself
entries.detail: One axiom on cascade:HealthRecord fixes this transitively and is the cheaper repair -- a class named HealthRecord asserting it bears record data is not a stretch.

A genuine question rather than an oversight, and spec#50 poses it rather than presuming: either the rule widens to include prov:Agent, or this class takes a second superclass, or it is deliberately outside the population and spec says so. It is stored in a pod either way, which is why it is here meanwhile.
Same open question as ProxyAgent, with a different foreign superclass.

No class index contains it under any rule. jayostis/spec#30 says it is a value rather than a record type, so the likely outcome is that this SDK stops registering it -- and then this entry goes without spec changing anything. Tracked here rather than in spec#50, which explicitly excludes it.
